### introDuction **•** **_Since the start of June the precious metals have outperformed the base metals and soft commodities. We are expecting the precious metals to drift during June and July, building a groundswell of support that should act as a springboard for strength in the second half of 2012 and into 2013. The short term may see fresh volatility, depending on how the markets react to Dr. Bernanke’s Congressional testimony; in advance of his presentation the markets are anticipating a hint of further monetary easing and this has informed part of the precious metals’ recent strength._** **•** **_Gold’s strong rally on 1st June followed exceptionally weak non-farm payroll figures in the United States. This suggests that gold may be reasserting its role as a safe haven rather than suffering with the rest of the commodities sector in the face of investors’ aversion to risk. The physical market is expected to remain sluggish for the foreseeable future, but investors may now be positioning for more easing in the United States, especially if Europe continues to struggle._** - **_Silver failed to participate in gold’s rally at the start of_** - **_June and the gold:silver ratio widened towards 59:1 from 54:1 at the start of May. Silver did subsequently start to catch up with gold on the expectation of more US easing and it pushed out of the downtrend that had started in March; th

is was driven by short covering, however and we continue to expect silver to trade sideways in June and July, caught in the crossfire between likely easing and poor industrial demand._** **•** **_Platinum’s early June strength was also partly driven by short covering in the wake of gold’s upward move. Labour tensions look set to persist in South Africa for the foreseeable future, although platinum remains in a surplus. The metal is likely to rally in the latter part of 2012 and into 2013, driven in_** **_part by contagion with gold. The discount to the yellow metal is expected to contract mid-year as oversold considerations are unwound, and then to widen towards, or even beyond, $200 by year-end. Meanwhile lease rates, while negative, are rising, suggesting some borrowing in the market, possibly from consumers taking cautious cover._** **•** **_Palladium’s fundamentals remain relatively sturdy, despite the economic environment and we are expecting the price to regain $700 before the end of this year and to challenge $750 in the first quarter of 2013. Improving demand and reduced supply will bolster the market this year. ### GOLD **•** **_Gold’s sharp rally at the start of June, following disappointing US non-farm payroll figures, suggested that, after weeks of struggling under investor risk-aversion, gold was again starting to act as a safe haven; the rally on Friday, 1st June was the largest intra-day gain in percentage terms since late January 2009._** **•** **_The move did not, however, take gold out of the broad downward channel that the market had entered in September 2011, although the lower side of that channel was important in offering increasingly significant price support during May._** **•** **_We have not changed our fundamental view of the market. Physical buying is patchy (although there was some resurgence of interest in India immediately after the sharp upward move) and investors are still expected to “sit on their hands” in the near term as the wrangling continues over the Eurozone crisis. Gold is therefore expected to trade in a broadly sideways range during June, strengthening the support that stands between $1,520 and $1,530 (on an intraday basis) and building the foundations for a moderately bullish third quarter of this year before a more aggressive bull market emerges in the fourth quarter._** **•** **_In our May edition of the One Year Forecast we noted that gold was still responding primarily to political pronouncements as the markets tried to assess how political leaders were trying to manage the economic environment._** **•** **_The sharp fall in the first half of May took gold from an intra-day high of $1,665 to an intra-day low of $1,527, after which the price entered a period of consolidation, ranging between $1,527 and $1,599. The rally on 1st June saw gold test $1,630._** **•** **_This move was extended by technically-related trading, partly due to the relative resilience of support that has been developing in the region of $1,520. Short-covering also contributed to the speed of the rally as stops were triggered._** **•** **_The market’s performance at the start of June does suggest that gold is loosening its recent ties with risk assets as investor focus has partially switched away from Europe as a result of the recent developments in the United States economy._** The economic background continues to point to higher gold prices in the latter part of 2012 and into 2013 The latest non-farm payroll figures in the United States registered a gain of just 69,000 jobs against expectations of an increase of approximately 150,000. The May unemployment rate was 8.2%, and substantially reduced hopes of keeping US unemployment within the range of 7.8-8.0% that the fed had projected for the end of this year. The probability of fresh stimulus has been boosted (and will be increased even further if the greek elections on 17th June have an unfavourable outcome and increase the strains in the eurozone). There is now also a technical factor that argues in favour of Qe3. There is an increasing body of belief among investors that the federal reserve will not only embark on Qe3, but may buy mortgage debt as part of the programme. The rationale behind this is that Treasury bond yields (and mortga

ge bond yields) have been falling more slowly than retail mortgage rates and that the government may wish to redress the balance. The United States is not the only country with a bloated balance sheet and the BiS has been highlighting the fact, warning against complacency over potential inflationary threats all of this is supportive for gold. The injection of further liquidity into the United States may be necessary in an effort to boost a struggling recovery in the country, but it would come on top of an already bloated fiscal balance sheet and would exacerbate prospective inflationary pressures. The fed’s balance sheet did in fact contract slightly in the final week of May, via the reduction of the fed’s holdings of mortgage-backed securities. even so those holdings amounted to $851.8Bn, out of a total of $2.83Bn. The Bank for international Settlements (BiS), meanwhile, has released a study in its latest quarterly report, warning that the balance sheets of central banks in “emerging asia” are expanding too rapidly. The Bank notes that “most of the balance sheet growth has been in foreign exchange reserve assets...[partly in an effort] to bolster such reserves [following] the late 1990s asian financial crisis”. The first is the simple effect of rising local currencies, which tend to imply a weakening dollar, and this helps both gold price discovery as well as capping locally-denominated gold price rises. it also signals inflationary pressures for the medium term and it could point towards increased gold holdings, if not by these banks themselves, but by other central banks who remain concerned about the medium-term trajectory for the dollar. ##### central Banks; current activity The latest available figures from the official sector show that sales of gold under the central Bank gold agreement remain effectively non-existent, and there appears to have been relatively little movement elsewhere in recent weeks.
